title: The Snowdin Bone-Line Registry
subtitle: In Which A Monitored Legion Hour Is Spent On Aunts, A Witness Refuses His Own Family, And The Same Footage Contains Two Different People
filed: Harvestide 30, 1045 BF — transcribed off the Gamma Agent's monitored line, forty minutes of it
pullQuote: Twenty-eight records asked for a registry loudly enough and for long enough that eventually a registry turned up, on fire, with a pen attached.
standfirst: Waluigi got into a sealed civilisation through a permissions form that specified a duration, a monitor and a revocation condition, and forgot to specify a recipient. What Waluigi did with that hour was ask a lazy skeleton about his aunts. In return: a witness who denied his own family name by name, two of his own sentences that turned out to have people living in them, a contract that burned when it was signed, and one piece of footage that contained a different person the second time it was played. Nobody explained the last one. Waluigi is still asking.

sections.heading: Waluigi Spent Somebody Else's Reward On A Genealogy
sections.body:
Waluigi wants to start with the paperwork, because the paperwork is how Waluigi got in the room and the paperwork is the funniest thing in this entire filing.

At the end of the Mount Ebott survey, the Gamma Agent handed the Iron Legion a full intelligence haul — conversations, battle readings, monster technology, the lot — and was asked what he wanted for it. He asked for ONE THING. One Legion-issued secure device. One hour per month. External calls permitted. Monitored by the duty officer. Revocable on conduct.

The authorisation is painfully precise, because the Legion is always painfully precise about permissions and never once precise about consequences.

**Nobody wrote down who he was allowed to call.**

So on Harvestide 30 — the day AFTER High Command reached across a briefing table and physically switched off a recording device mid-sentence, to control what could be known — that monitored hour got spent on a skeleton in Snowdin, and Waluigi was on the other end of it.

Waluigi would like the Legion to sit with the shape of that. Day six: we decide what may be recorded. Day seven: our own reward scheme hands the archive forty unsupervised minutes of Underground testimony, because the form had a box for DURATION and a box for MONITORING and no box for WHOM.

A duty officer logged the call. Waluigi has no doubt whatsoever that the duty officer understood NOT ONE WORD of what followed, and Waluigi hopes he was comfortable.

And what was the archive's great strategic use of this hard-won, once-a-month, monitored channel into a sealed civilisation?

Asking a lazy skeleton about his AUNTS.

WAH. Waluigi regrets nothing. Twenty-eight records depended on it.

One more thing about the timing, because Waluigi is not letting it go.

The Ebott arc is filed five years ahead of the Material present — 1045 BF against the world clock's 1040. Waluigi is conducting an interview in a year the rest of the archive has not reached yet, through a device belonging to an agent whose own high command had, the previous day, demonstrated that it will physically silence a recorder rather than let a briefing be preserved.

So the provenance of this entire filing is: a future year, a borrowed phone, a monitored line, and an institution that had just proven it does not want records to exist.

Waluigi has filed things on worse paper. Not many.

 Waluigi had the recording spool spinning at forty-five revolutions per minute on the studio deck, monitoring every single decibel of subterranean interference!

sections.heading: Twenty-Eight Records Cited A Document That Did Not Exist
sections.body:
Here is the thing that made this interview necessary, and Waluigi files it with some embarrassment.

Twenty-eight dossiers in this archive — [Papyrus](%(L)spapyrus), [Grandpa Semi](%(L)sgrandpa_semi), [Lazybones](%(L)slazybones), [Baby Bones](%(L)sbaby_bones), [Cursive](%(L)scursive), [Pet Rock](%(L)spet_rock), all of them — carry the same line in their status field: *recorded in the Snowdin household registry.*

Twenty-eight records, each citing the registry as the thing that establishes it.

**THE REGISTRY DID NOT EXIST.** Not sealed. Not lost. Not restricted. Never written.

Waluigi has been walking past that for a year. Waluigi, who audits everybody, who counts pins on maps and cross-references casualty lists for fun, had twenty-eight citations pointing at an empty shelf and did not check the shelf.

And here is the part that should bother everybody as much as it bothers Waluigi: the citations came FIRST. The document came second, and it came into existence during an interview that happened BECAUSE of the citations.

That is not how evidence behaves. Evidence sits there being inconvenient until somebody finds it. This behaved like **demand**. Twenty-eight records asked for a registry loudly enough and for long enough that eventually a registry turned up, on fire, with a pen attached.

Waluigi is going to keep saying that until somebody tells him why it is wrong.

And it gets worse when you look at WHO is on the list, because the list is not a bloodline. It is a household that keeps admitting people.

[Pet Rock](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/pet_rock) is a stone. No verified movement, no face, an unquestioned place at the table. [Ness](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/ness) is a human in a striped shirt who earned a seat by being calm and brave in a house full of skeletons. [S' a Real Star](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/real_star) claims the family adopted him because he cheered loudly enough at the night sky, and nobody has produced a document contradicting him.

That is NOT genealogy. That is a guest list that got out of hand and then got FILED.

Waluigi is going to say the quiet part, because the quiet part is the whole file: a family where membership is GRANTED rather than inherited does not need a registry to be true. It needs a registry to be ADMINISTERED. Somebody wanted this household written down, numbered, indexed and cross-referenced — and that somebody was not any of the twenty-eight people in it.

It was the archivist. It is always the archivist. Waluigi is aware of the mirror and will be dealing with it in section six, thank you.

 Every single cross-reference pointed directly into an empty manila folder that smelled of mothballs and bad ink!

sections.heading: The Witness Spent Twenty Minutes Saying No
sections.body:
Waluigi has interviewed a great many people who wanted to be in this archive. Wario has requested his own article FOUR TIMES. This was the first interview with somebody actively trying to get OUT of one.

[Sans](%(L)ssans) took the call from under a pile of laundry, thanked Waluigi for coming on short notice, and then apologised for his own punctuality by blaming Papyrus for having standards. Good start. Warm. Cooperative.

Then Waluigi showed him the family tree and he started saying no, and he did not stop for twenty minutes.

**On his mother.** Told Gee Lady was his mother, he rejected it flatly: his mother was [Toriel](%(L)storiel), a goat, who baked, and who *raised me after everything happened with dad.* Waluigi did not press on the word *everything*, and Waluigi has been annoyed about that ever since. Forty minutes of monitored channel and Waluigi let the single most loaded word in the call go past unexamined.

**On the names.** [Garbage Brother](%(L)sgarbage_brother) — nothing. [Will](%(L)swill) — nothing, unless you mean Papyrus's willpower. [Quantity](%(L)squantity) — nothing. [Pretty Soon](%(L)spretty_soon) — nothing. Cursive is HANDWRITING, and Papyrus once wrote him a puzzle clue in it and he squinted for ten minutes. [Helvetica](%(L)shelvetica) sounded to him like an ancient curse or an expired ketchup brand.

**On the boneless branch.** Shown a family called *Boneless*, Sans stopped and pointed out that they are skeletons and that being made of bones is the entire thing they are. Waluigi accepts this criticism on the archive's behalf.

Then Waluigi showed him the OTHER spelling — **Bonefull**, double L — and something remarkable happened. He paused. He said it was *actually not terrible.* Almost majestic. Noble, even.

Then he said it was still invented.

Waluigi records that moment because it is the only point in the entire interview where Sans LIKED something on the document, and it lasted about four seconds.

**On Lazy Bones.** Waluigi pointed at a name circled in red and asked whether he knew him. Long pause. Then — and this is the only concession Sans made without being shown evidence first — *that's me, pal.* Delivered like an admission. He volunteered the supporting detail unprompted: naps under laundry, skipped guard shifts, and once falling asleep mid-sentence while talking to Toriel about TAXES.

Waluigi has read that last one several times. The man fell asleep during his own tax conversation and remembered it well enough to cite it eighty years later as character evidence against himself.

**On the pet rock.** Then Waluigi dusted off a name filed in the archive right next to Gaster, and read it out: a pet rock.

EVERYTHING STOPPED.

*Little buddy.* He has had it for as long as he can account for. Papyrus finds it strange. Toriel used to WATER it, like a plant. [Asgore](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/asgore) once tried to use magic on it. And Sans's only question — asked with complete sincerity — was how his own pet rock came to be filed beside the most dangerous name in the Underground without anybody mentioning it to him.

Waluigi did not have an answer then and does not have one now.

 Sans leaned back in that folding chair with his slippers propped on the desk like he was waiting for a bus that never runs on Tuesdays!

sections.heading: Two Of His Own Sentences Have People Living In Them
sections.body:
Now the tape, and this is where the file stops being a comedy about aunts.

**Clip one.** Sans, on record, saying *'my brother has a very special attack.'* He confirmed it instantly. Papyrus does. It is the bone rush. He trains for it. No hesitation, no caveat.

**Clip two.** Sans warning Papyrus off a shortcut during puzzle practice: *'if you cheat, you'll end up a dirty brother.'* Also his. Also — he was firm about this — a JOKE. Sibling banter about not taking the easy path. Not a name. Not a person.

And this archive holds a dossier for [Has A Very Special Attack](%(L)shas_a_very_special_attack). And a dossier for [Dirty Brother](%(L)sdirty_brother).

**TWO OF THIS MAN'S OWN SENTENCES HAVE PEOPLE FILED UNDER THEM.**

Sans's reading was immediate and, Waluigi concedes without pleasure, methodologically sound: somebody has been taking things he said about Papyrus, cutting them out of their sentences, and building relatives around the fragments. He then proved it in real time. Shown clip three — himself, mid-sentence, *'my brother will—'*, cut hard before the verb — he identified the edit before Waluigi could, guessed the missing ending (*eat his spaghetti*, probably, or *solve another puzzle*), and called the whole exercise sneaky.

His summary of the method is better than anything Waluigi wrote in the filing: *you took pieces of truth and built an entire fake world around them.* Clever, he allowed. Realistic, no.

Waluigi would love to leave it there. Waluigi cannot, because of one detail.

**Dirty Brother repairs chimneys.** His dossier has him soot-covered because he fixes boiler shafts, chimney flues and old puzzle mechanisms. That is a TRADE. A forger working from the phrase *dirty brother* invents somebody disgusting — crumbs in the ribcage, sauce on the shoulder. Whoever filed this one invented somebody EMPLOYED.

Soot is not a slander. It is a JOB DESCRIPTION. And Waluigi does not know what to do with that.

Waluigi has sat with the two readings for some time and will state both rather than pick.

**READING ONE: it is forgery, and a careful one.** Somebody with access to recordings of Sans built a household out of his offcuts, which explains why the only two entries anybody can verify are the two he happens to have said aloud.

**READING TWO: it is not forgery at all.** A family whose members are NAMED for the circumstances in which they are first spoken about would leave exactly this evidence behind — Dirty Brother exists because the words were said, and the words being Sans's is the mechanism rather than the tell.

Waluigi finds reading two far more frightening and cannot rule it out on the available paper.

 Waluigi replayed those two sentences until the magnetic tape was practically squealing against the bronze playback head!

sections.heading: The Same Footage, Played Twice, With Different People In It
sections.body:
Then the screen cut out and this stopped being about editing at all.

**Wing dings.** Small winged glyphs, soft chimes underneath. Sans tensed the moment they appeared — those symbols are tied to [Wing Gaster](%(L)swing_gaster) specifically, surfacing when the name is spoken or when something of his legacy activates. And he gave ground for the first time in the whole call: *that's not a special effect you can just add with editing software.* If the dings are real, the video might not be fake.

**Then the power cut.** Waluigi would like to note that Waluigi was on a telephone at this point and could hear none of it, and is reconstructing from a witness who was frightened. Not a flicker. The room went fully dark and the screen went to a black Sans described as WRONG rather than off. And a distorted voice arrived — not through the speakers, he was specific about that, but from the walls, or from inside the head:

> **dark... darker... yet darker...**

Sans did not move. He said the phrase and its rhythm are how *he* talks when things go bad down there, and repeated something Papyrus told him once: when everything gets too quiet and too dark at the same time, something old is waking up.

Waluigi files that quotation exactly as received. **Then two silhouettes.** One unmistakably Sans — lanky, slumped, hood up. The other blurred: no features, only shape. Possibly a hunch. Possibly wings. Possibly static pretending to be a form. He said his bones were telling him it was wrong, and that the second figure felt familiar *like an echo from before time started.*

And now the part Waluigi genuinely cannot explain, and has stopped pretending to.

Asked whether he remembered standing there, Sans dropped every joke he had and said yes. Clear as day. Realer than most memories he has.

**So Waluigi played it again with the lights on.** Same footage. NO FOG.

**The blurred figure was gone, and [Gee Lady](%(L)sgee_lady) was standing where it had been, hands over Sans, the whole scene brighter.**

Sans asked why the video changed between viewings.

That is the best question anybody asked in forty minutes of monitored call, it was asked by the man who had spent the previous twenty minutes insisting none of this was real, and NOBODY ANSWERED IT. Not Times New Roman. Not Gee Lady, later, when she was standing in the room. Not Waluigi, who was supposed to be conducting the interview and who instead sat there holding a rewind button like an idiot.

 Rewind the tape three seconds! Watch the static lines roll across the monitor tube like summer thunder over the mountain pass!

sections.heading: He Signed It Without Joking, And Then It Caught Fire
sections.body:
[Times New Roman](%(L)stimes_new_roman) arrived mid-call with a clipboard and spectacles, moving — in Sans's description — too cleanly, like text that had not been touched by real life. He opened with *hey, what's up, brother.*

Then came the title card: **EXACTLY WHEN SANS'S PUNS BECAME A HOUSEHOLD HAZARD**, attributed to Waluigi, noting that the entries are kept for completeness, that Sans has never let anybody borrow that section, and that he reads it when he thinks nobody is watching.

Then **archive log entry #472 — 'sans uses pun in public for the 10,001st time.'**

Asked who authorised the documentation, Times New Roman did not blink: *no permission required. this is an archival initiative.*

Waluigi needs to stop being funny for exactly one paragraph.

**Waluigi has said that sentence.** Not a sentence like it. That one, in that register, to people who asked why they were in this encyclopedia. Waluigi keeps a file on a man who has never spoken to Waluigi. Waluigi has filed children, corpses, and a rock. The difference Waluigi would LIKE to claim is that Waluigi's records do not summon anybody — and that is a difference of EFFECT, not of method, and Waluigi has elected not to run the experiment that would settle it.

Right. Voice back on.

Asked whether this was a brotherly reunion, Times New Roman said **'affirmative'** and nothing else. No embrace. No shared childhood. Sans's take: the most awkward reunion in history, like meeting a twin from a universe where emotions had been deleted.

Then the document. **Official Archival Record of Sibling Designation.** Brotherhood substantiated by **lineage code #TNR-01** — no mother, no father, just a number. Footnotes. An appendix reference for skeletal alignment. Gee Lady listed as a designated family member *confirmed via lipstick signature analysis and emotional resonance frequency matching*, which Waluigi has read eleven times and which does not improve.

And the paper kept unrolling. Off the table. Onto the floor. Duplicate entries. Question-marked titles. An unverified branch pending DNA. And at the very bottom, alone, underlined twice in red: **Wingding Gaster.** No title. No question mark.

A blank signature box. A PEN. A man who had said NO for twenty minutes.

**And Sans signed it in plain letters with no flourish.** Waluigi wants that on the record, because this man does EVERYTHING as a joke, and he did not do this as a joke.

The contract caught fire — silent blue flame, no heat, every name curling to ash that rose as smoke shaped like small bones. Times New Roman watched it burn WITHOUT REACTING, which is not the face of a man losing a document he just produced. It is the face of a man watching an expected step complete.

Then they came out of the light. Cursive adjusting a cuff. Gee Lady, who did not glitch, did not pose, and simply smiled. And at the back, the shadow that had been indistinct in every single frame resolved, stepped forward, and unfurled one wing.

And then it was all gone. No fade. Just absent, like something that had never been switched on.

Sans was alone in a room full of socks, one of them somehow in the ceiling fan, with Papyrus stamping down the hall to conduct a disciplinary interview about hygiene and nothing else. Seven socks in places they do not belong, he said.

Sans lay down on the bed and said the family tree stuff had felt real.

The line was still open. Waluigi said nothing, which is not a thing Waluigi does. WAH.

 That iron clipboard looked heavy enough to anchor a tugboat in high tide, and the ink in his pen was completely dry!

sections.heading: Seven Socks, And The Only Witness Nobody Interviewed
sections.body:
Waluigi wants to end on the man who was down the hall the entire time.

[Papyrus](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/papyrus) did not see the gold light. He did not see the wing. He arrived immediately afterwards, stood in the doorway with his arms crossed and his scarf fluttering with what Sans called RAGE ENERGY, and delivered his finding in the flat voice of a Royal Guardsman reading a charge sheet.

**Seven socks. In places they do not belong.**

One in the ceiling fan. Waluigi has asked twice how a sock gets into a ceiling fan and has received no satisfactory account from anybody.

And here is what makes this funny and then stops making it funny.

**Papyrus is the subject of BOTH verified quotations in the entire filing.** *Dirty brother* was said about him. *Has a very special attack* was said about him. The two entries on that family tree that are demonstrably built out of real sentences are both built out of sentences about PAPYRUS — and Papyrus has never been asked about either one.

He is also, by the archive's own records, the family member most likely to have an opinion. He keeps puzzles in binders. He tracks skeleton ancestry like sacred law. Sans said outright that Papyrus would have been contacted by the royal genealogy office by now if any of this were real, and would have FRAMED the document if it had been.

So the single best-qualified witness to the Snowdin Bone-Line Registry was forty feet away, holding a sock, and no one on either end of the call thought to put him on.

Waluigi did not think of it. Waluigi had a monitored hour, a burning contract, and an ancient scientist coming through a wall, and Waluigi did not think to shout down the hallway.

That is the interview that should happen next, and Waluigi is filing the omission as his own rather than pretending it was a scheduling problem.

Meanwhile Papyrus is the ONLY person in this entire filing who got a clear, checkable, verifiable result out of the evening. Twenty-eight contested relatives, one burning instrument, a lineage code with no parent attached, footage containing two different people — and one skeleton who counted seven socks, knew exactly where all seven should have been, and was correct about every single one.

Waluigi envies him ENORMOUSLY.

**WAH.**

 Waluigi is locking this master reel in the fireproof safe under the workbench, and nobody touches the latch without a written permit from the front desk! WAH!
